newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian parliament speaker offers to quit.
newsitem.headline: Armenian parliament speaker offers to quit.

text.p: The speaker of the Armenian parliament, Babken Ararktsyan, tendered his resignation on Wednesday after the assembly adopted a law on extending military conscription which he strongly opposed.

Ararktsyan told the chamber that the Defence Ministry had "applied pressure to parliament" to adopt a law that all men must enter the armed forces of the former Soviet republic at 18, dropping exclusions previously granted for students.

Ararktsyan, a close ally of President Levon Ter-Petrosyan, said he "did not have the power to resist the pressure" from the Defence Ministry. "Either that, or I don't understand how the republic should work," he told deputies.
Parliament will convene later on Wednesday to discuss whether to accept his resignation.

Ararktsyan had argued that students in further education should not be conscripted. The law had been approved by Ter-Petrosyan and was due to come into force in late 1998. Armenia is involved in a protracted dispute with neighbour Azerbaijan over territory around the Nagorno-Karabakh region.
Ter-Petrosyan signed a decree on Tuesday combining four economic ministries into two and dismissing his economy minister and industry minister.
